cccma_ppp.generic.monitoring module

class cccma_ppp.generic.monitoring.Monitor(*, cpu: bool = True, ram: bool = True, gpu0: bool = False, gpu1: bool = False, gpus: Iterable[int] | None = None, interval: float = 0.1, rank: int = 0, local_rank: int = 0, world_size: int = 1)

Bases: object

Monitor process resource utilization and execution stages.

Resource samples are collected periodically in a background thread and can include process CPU usage, resident memory, and utilization and memory usage for selected GPUs. Named spans and checkpoints can be recorded alongside resource samples to associate utilization with execution stages.

Parameters:

  • cpu (bool) – Whether to collect process CPU utilization.

  • ram (bool) – Whether to collect process resident memory usage.

  • gpu0 (bool) – Whether to monitor physical GPU index 0.

  • gpu1 (bool) – Whether to monitor physical GPU index 1.

  • gpus (Iterable[int] | None) – Additional physical GPU indices to monitor.

  • interval (float) – Sampling interval in seconds.

  • rank (int) – Global rank associated with the monitored process.

  • local_rank (int) – Local rank associated with the monitored process.

  • world_size (int) – Number of processes participating in the distributed execution.

checkpoint(name: str) → None

Record an instantaneous named checkpoint.

The checkpoint name is qualified by the currently active monitoring stage when applicable.

Parameters:

name (str) – Name of the checkpoint.

Raises:

  • TypeError – If name is not a string.

  • ValueError – If name is empty after removing surrounding whitespace.

clear() → None

Remove all recorded monitoring events.

close() → None

Stop resource monitoring and release GPU-monitoring resources.

Return the active monitoring stage for the current thread.

Returns:

Name of the innermost active stage, or "root" if no monitoring span is active.

Return type:

str

plot(df: Any = None, metrics: Iterable[str] | None = None, save_path: str | PathLike[str] | None = None, show: bool = True, smooth: str | None = None, **smooth_kwargs: Any)

Plot resource utilization together with the execution timeline.

Resource samples are displayed in separate metric panels while completed spans and checkpoints are shown on a timeline. Metrics may optionally be smoothed before display.

Parameters:

  • df (Any) – Monitoring dataframe to plot. If None, recorded monitoring events are used.

  • metrics (Iterable[str] | None) – Resource metrics to plot. If None, all collected metrics containing valid data are selected.

  • save_path (str | os.PathLike[str] | None) – Path at which to save the generated figure.

  • show (bool) – Whether to display the figure interactively.

  • smooth (str | None) – Optional smoothing method applied to plotted metric values.

  • **smooth_kwargs (Any) – Additional arguments passed to the selected smoothing method.

Returns:

Generated Matplotlib figure, or None if there are no events or no usable resource samples to plot.

Return type:

Any

Raises:

  • TypeError – If metrics is provided as a single string instead of an iterable of metric names.

  • ValueError – If required dataframe columns are missing or a requested metric was not collected.

property running: bool

Indicate whether the background monitoring thread is running.

Returns:

True while the monitoring thread is alive, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

span(name: str) → Iterator

Record a named execution span.

Spans may be nested. Their full names reflect the nesting hierarchy, and matching start and end events share a unique span identifier.

Parameters:

name (str) – Name of the execution span.

Yields:

None – Control to the code executed within the monitored span.

Raises:

  • TypeError – If name is not a string.

  • ValueError – If name is empty after removing surrounding whitespace.

start(*, clear: bool = False) → None

Start resource monitoring in a background thread.

Parameters:

clear (bool) – Whether to remove previously recorded monitoring events before starting.

stop(timeout: float | None = None) → None

Stop the background monitoring thread.

Parameters:

timeout (float | None) – Maximum number of seconds to wait for the monitoring thread to terminate. If None, waits until the thread exits.

Raises:

ValueError – If timeout is negative.

cccma_ppp.generic.monitoring.build_distributed_monitor(distributed: Distributed, *, cpu: bool = True, ram: bool = True, gpu: bool = True, interval: float = 0.1) → Monitor

Build a resource monitor for a distributed process.

When GPU monitoring is enabled, the process’s local CUDA rank is resolved to a physical GPU index for NVML monitoring. Failure to resolve the GPU does not disable CPU or RAM monitoring.

Parameters:

  • distributed (Distributed) – Distributed runtime containing rank, local-rank, and world-size information.

  • cpu (bool) – Whether to collect process CPU utilization.

  • ram (bool) – Whether to collect process resident memory usage.

  • gpu (bool) – Whether to monitor the GPU assigned to the distributed process.

  • interval (float) – Sampling interval in seconds.

Returns:

Resource monitor configured for the distributed process.

Return type:

Monitor

cccma_ppp.generic.monitoring.combine_rank_results(output_dir: str | PathLike[str], world_size: int) → Path | None

Combine resource-monitoring CSV files from multiple ranks.

Available rank files are concatenated and, when possible, sorted by timestamp and rank before being written to a combined CSV file.

Parameters:

  • output_dir (str | os.PathLike[str]) – Directory containing per-rank monitoring CSV files.

  • world_size (int) – Number of distributed ranks expected to have produced monitoring files.

Returns:

Path to the combined CSV file, or None if no rank files are found.

Return type:

Path | None

Raises:

  • TypeError – If world_size is not an integer.

  • ValueError – If world_size is not positive.

cccma_ppp.generic.monitoring.distributed_monitoring(distributed: Distributed, output_dir: str | os.PathLike[str], *, cpu: bool = True, ram: bool = True, gpu: bool = True, interval: float = 0.1, combine_ranks: bool = True) → Iterator

Monitor resources within a distributed execution context.

Monitoring starts when the context is entered and records whether execution completed or was interrupted. Results are exported when leaving the context. After successful completion, ranks synchronize and the root process can combine per-rank monitoring results.

Parameters:

  • distributed (Distributed) – Distributed runtime associated with the monitored process.

  • output_dir (str | os.PathLike[str]) – Directory in which monitoring results are written.

  • cpu (bool) – Whether to collect process CPU utilization.

  • ram (bool) – Whether to collect process resident memory usage.

  • gpu (bool) – Whether to monitor the GPU assigned to each distributed process.

  • interval (float) – Sampling interval in seconds.

  • combine_ranks (bool) – Whether the root process combines per-rank CSV files after successful completion.

Yields:

Monitor – Active resource monitor for the current distributed process.

cccma_ppp.generic.monitoring.export_results(resource_monitor: Monitor, output_dir: str | PathLike[str]) → tuple[Path | None, Path | None]

Export resource-monitoring data and visualization for one rank.

Recorded events are written to CSV and plotted using Kalman-smoothed resource metrics.

Parameters:

  • resource_monitor (Monitor) – Resource monitor containing the events to export.

  • output_dir (str | os.PathLike[str]) – Directory in which the CSV and plot are saved.

Returns:

Paths to the exported CSV file and plot, or (None, None) when no monitoring data were collected.

Return type:

tuple[Path | None, Path | None]

cccma_ppp.generic.monitoring.resolve_physical_gpu_index(local_rank: int) → int

Resolve a local CUDA rank to its physical GPU index.

When CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is unset, the local rank is treated as the physical GPU index. Numeric visible-device entries are resolved directly, while GPU UUIDs are matched against physical devices through NVML.

Parameters:

local_rank (int) – Zero-based local CUDA rank to resolve.

Returns:

Physical GPU index corresponding to local_rank.

Return type:

int

Raises:

  • TypeError – If local_rank is not an integer.

  • ValueError – If local_rank is negative or outside the visible-device range, a visible-device identifier is unsupported, or a GPU UUID cannot be resolved through NVML.
